fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique bus identifier. Every component attached to the bus names it, so a rename re-points them all.

fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: Energy carrier modelled at this bus (AC, DC, H2, heat, gas, …). It decides which assets can attach and which energy balance the bus enters.

fields.label: Control
fields.help: Power-flow control for the non-linear AC power flow: PQ (a load), PV (regulated voltage) or Slack (the reference). For the linear optimisation only the slack matters.

fields.label: Country
fields.help: ISO country code, for grouping, country-level statistics and policy constraints.

fields.label: Unit
fields.help: What the bus carries, for a product bus: MWh for an energy product (H2, NH3) or t for a material (ore, concentrate). Empty for an electrical bus, which reads as MW.

fields.label: Energy per tonne
fields.help: For an energy product in MWh: its lower heating value, which results use to show tonnes (NH3: 5.166 MWh/t). Empty: tonnes are Unavailable.

fields.label: Product value
fields.help: What one unit of this product is worth to the client, per the bus's unit (EUR/MWh or EUR/t), with its source in the ledger. Results value a process unit's output at it. Empty: that value is Unavailable, never 0.

fields.label: Sub-network
fields.help: Manual region label for the 'region' clustering mode: buses sharing it collapse to one node. Empty: determined from the electrical topology.

fields.label: Longitude
fields.help: Geographic longitude, east positive. Places the bus on the map and sets the length of a line recalculated from coordinates; the optimisation does not read it.

fields.label: Latitude
fields.help: Geographic latitude, north positive. Places the bus on the map and sets the length of a line recalculated from coordinates; the optimisation does not read it.

fields.label: Nominal voltage
fields.help: The bus's nominal voltage. Lines are coloured by voltage class; a transformer's declared voltages are checked against it.

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique carrier name. Buses and assets name it; a rename re-points them.

fields.label: Display name
fields.help: How the carrier is shown in charts and tables. Empty: its name.

fields.label: Colour
fields.help: Its colour on the map and in charts, as a CSS colour (e.g. #1f77b4).

fields.label: Unit
fields.help: Unit of the energy it carries, for display. Empty: MWh.

fields.label: CO₂ emissions
fields.help: Emissions per MWh of primary energy burnt. A generator's emissions are this divided by its efficiency; a CO₂ cap sums them.

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique generator identifier. Time-series profiles are matched to this exact name.

fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: Technology carrier (solar, onwind, OCGT, …). Drives CO₂ accounting, grouping and canvas colours.

fields.label: Bus
fields.help: Bus the generator injects into.

fields.label: Capacity
fields.help: Installed active-power capacity. With extendable ticked, the existing capacity the optimiser starts from.

fields.label: Extendable
fields.help: When ticked, the optimiser chooses the capacity between the minimum and maximum and pays the annualised cost for every MW it adds.

fields.label: Minimum capacity
fields.help: Lower bound on the optimised capacity. Set it to the existing capacity to forbid retirement.

fields.label: Maximum capacity
fields.help: Upper bound on the optimised capacity. Leave empty for no limit.

fields.label: Overnight cost
fields.help: Upfront cost per unit of capacity, as if built at once without financing. Annualised over the lifetime at the discount rate.

fields.label: Lifetime
fields.help: Technical and economic lifetime. The asset retires after its build year plus lifetime.

fields.label: Build year
fields.help: First year the asset operates. With its lifetime, it decides in which investment periods the asset exists.

fields.label: Discount rate
fields.help: The rate this asset's overnight cost is annualised at. Leave empty to use the project's rate from Solver Settings.

fields.label: Capital cost (annualised)
fields.help: Derived: overnight cost × annuity(discount rate, lifetime); fixed O&M is charged on top. The optimiser pays it on every MW it adds, for the share of a year your snapshots represent.

fields.label: Fixed O&M
fields.help: Fixed operation and maintenance per installed unit per year, paid on the whole capacity whatever the dispatch.

fields.label: Marginal cost
fields.help: Variable cost per MWh dispatched: fuel plus variable O&M.

fields.label: Curtailment cost
fields.help: Penalty per MWh of available but unused energy. Set above zero to discourage spilling wind or solar.

fields.label: Start-up cost
fields.help: Cost of one start-up.

fields.label: Shut-down cost
fields.help: Cost of one shut-down.

fields.label: Efficiency
fields.help: Conversion efficiency from primary energy to electricity. Used for CO₂ accounting (carrier emissions ÷ efficiency).

fields.label: Minimum output
fields.help: Minimum dispatch as a share of capacity: a must-run floor.

fields.label: Availability
fields.help: Maximum dispatch as a share of capacity. For wind and solar, the time-varying capacity factor uploaded as a profile.

fields.label: Unit commitment
fields.help: Model on/off decisions with start-ups and minimum up and down times. Adds integer variables: slower, more realistic for thermal plants.

fields.label: Ramp-up limit
fields.help: Largest hour-on-hour increase, as a share of capacity per hour.

fields.label: Ramp-down limit
fields.help: Largest hour-on-hour decrease, as a share of capacity per hour.

fields.label: Minimum up time
fields.help: Hours the unit stays on after a start-up.

fields.label: Minimum down time
fields.help: Hours the unit stays off after a shut-down.

fields.label: Minimum energy
fields.help: Least energy the generator must produce over the modelled horizon (Σ dispatch × weight). Empty for no lower bound.

fields.label: Maximum energy
fields.help: Most energy the generator may produce over the modelled horizon, e.g. a fuel or water budget. Empty for no upper bound.

fields.label: AC control
fields.help: Control type in the AC power flow only: PQ fixes P and Q, PV holds the voltage, Slack absorbs the imbalance.

fields.label: Forced-outage rate
fields.help: Share of time the asset is out on a forced outage, e.g. 5 %. Empty uses the carrier's library default. Read by the adequacy and FMEA analysis only; the dispatch is unaffected.

fields.label: Outage-rate basis
fields.help: What the rate is: FOR (service-hours based, what NERC GADS class averages publish) or EFORd (demand based). They differ materially for peakers with reserve-shutdown hours; the tool stores which one you entered and never converts between them.

fields.label: Mean time to repair
fields.help: How long one forced outage lasts on average. With the rate it implies an event frequency (8760 × rate / MTTR per year).

fields.label: Availability includes outages
fields.help: Tick when the availability profile already accounts for forced outages (a historical capacity-factor table). The adequacy engines then apply no outage rate on top.

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique constraint name.

fields.label: Type
fields.help: What the constraint caps: primary energy (a CO₂ cap), new capacity of a carrier, a carrier's dispatch, or the volume or cost of new transmission.

fields.label: Sense
fields.help: How the sum compares with the constant.

fields.label: Constant
fields.help: The bound, in the type's unit: t for a CO₂ cap, MW for capacity, MWh for dispatch, MW·km or € for transmission.

fields.label: Carrier attribute
fields.help: For primary energy: the carrier column summed, e.g. co2_emissions.

fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: For a capacity or operational limit: the carrier it applies to.

fields.label: Investment period
fields.help: The period it binds in. Empty: the whole horizon.

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique line identifier.

fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: AC for an AC line. Used for grouping and canvas colours. A line joins buses of one carrier; join buses of different carriers with a Link.

fields.label: From bus
fields.help: The bus at one end. A positive flow in the results runs from this bus to the other.

fields.label: To bus
fields.help: The bus at the other end.

fields.label: Capacity
fields.help: Apparent-power rating of the line. With extendable ticked, the existing capacity the optimiser starts from.

fields.label: Extendable
fields.help: When ticked, the optimiser chooses the capacity between the minimum and maximum and pays the annualised cost for every MVA it adds.

fields.label: Minimum capacity
fields.help: Lower bound on the optimised capacity.

fields.label: Maximum capacity
fields.help: Upper bound on the optimised capacity. Leave empty for no limit.

fields.label: Length
fields.help: Route length. The impedances and the investment are entered per km and scale with it.

fields.label: Overnight cost per km
fields.help: Upfront cost per MVA of capacity and km of route, as catalogues publish it (e.g. HVAC overhead). Times the length, annualised over the lifetime at the discount rate.

fields.label: Lifetime
fields.help: Technical and economic lifetime. The line retires after its build year plus lifetime; leave empty for never.

fields.label: Build year
fields.help: First year the asset operates. With its lifetime, it decides in which investment periods the asset exists.

fields.label: Discount rate
fields.help: The rate this asset's overnight cost is annualised at. Leave empty to use the project's rate from Solver Settings.

fields.label: Capital cost (annualised)
fields.help: Derived: overnight cost per km × length × annuity(discount rate, lifetime); fixed O&M is charged on top. Per MVA of capacity.

fields.label: Fixed O&M
fields.help: Fixed operation and maintenance per year, as a share of the overnight cost.

fields.label: Fixed O&M (total)
fields.help: Derived: the overnight cost per km × length × the fixed O&M share, per MVA of capacity per year.

fields.label: Forced-outage rate
fields.help: Share of time the asset is out on a forced outage, e.g. 5 %. Empty uses the carrier's library default. Read by the adequacy and FMEA analysis only; the dispatch is unaffected.

fields.label: Outage-rate basis
fields.help: What the rate is: FOR (service-hours based, what NERC GADS class averages publish) or EFORd (demand based). They differ materially for peakers with reserve-shutdown hours; the tool stores which one you entered and never converts between them.

fields.label: Mean time to repair
fields.help: How long one forced outage lasts on average. With the rate it implies an event frequency (8760 × rate / MTTR per year).

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique link identifier. Time-series profiles are matched to this exact name.

fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: Technology carrier (electrolysis, fuel cell, DC, heat pump, …). Drives grouping and canvas colours.

fields.label: From bus
fields.help: Input side: the bus the link draws from. Its capacity and cost are per MW of this input.

fields.label: To bus
fields.help: Output side: the bus that receives the input × efficiency.

fields.label: Port 2 bus
fields.help: Optional extra port 2: with a positive efficiency2 the bus receives energy (CHP heat); with a negative one the link draws from it (a process feed). Leave empty for no port 2.

fields.label: Port 3 bus
fields.help: Optional extra port 3: with a positive efficiency3 the bus receives energy (CHP heat); with a negative one the link draws from it (a process feed). Leave empty for no port 3.

fields.label: Port 4 bus
fields.help: Optional extra port 4: with a positive efficiency4 the bus receives energy (CHP heat); with a negative one the link draws from it (a process feed). Leave empty for no port 4.

fields.label: Process unit
fields.help: Tick when this link is a production step: bus0 is the main input, bus1 the product, the other ports further inputs. A process unit is a fixed client input, not a decision of the plan.

fields.label: Criticality tier
fields.help: How this unit's electrical supply is ranked when it must be cut: safety (priced at VoLL), process_critical (a stop costs a restart), process_flexible (it can stop and catch up from inventory) or deferrable (it shifts within the day).

fields.label: Capacity
fields.help: Rating on the input side (bus0). With extendable ticked, the existing capacity the optimiser starts from.

fields.label: Extendable
fields.help: When ticked, the optimiser chooses the capacity between the minimum and maximum and pays the annualised cost for every MW it adds.

fields.label: Minimum capacity
fields.help: Lower bound on the optimised capacity. Set it to the existing capacity to forbid retirement.

fields.label: Maximum capacity
fields.help: Upper bound on the optimised capacity. Leave empty for no limit.

fields.label: Overnight cost
fields.help: Upfront cost per kW of input capacity, as if built at once without financing. Annualised over the lifetime at the discount rate.

fields.label: Lifetime
fields.help: Technical and economic lifetime. The link retires after its build year plus lifetime.

fields.label: Build year
fields.help: First year the asset operates. With its lifetime, it decides in which investment periods the asset exists.

fields.label: Discount rate
fields.help: The rate this asset's overnight cost is annualised at. Leave empty to use the project's rate from Solver Settings.

fields.label: Capital cost (annualised)
fields.help: Derived: overnight cost × annuity(discount rate, lifetime); fixed O&M is charged on top. Per kW of input.

fields.label: Fixed O&M
fields.help: Fixed operation and maintenance per kW of input per year.

fields.label: Marginal cost
fields.help: Cost per MWh drawn from the input bus.

fields.label: Start-up cost
fields.help: Read-only. PyPSA does not weight a start-up cost by the snapshot or period weighting, so a process unit prices a restart as lost production instead (see grid-to-process ticket 03).

fields.label: Stand-by cost
fields.help: Cost per hour while the unit is on, at any output, including zero.

fields.label: Efficiency
fields.help: Output per unit of input: MWh delivered to bus1 per MWh drawn from bus0 (the COP for a heat pump, above 100 %).

fields.label: Port 2 efficiency
fields.help: Flow on port 2 per unit drawn from bus0. Positive: the port bus receives it (CHP heat, 0.4 = 0.4 MWh per MWh of fuel). Negative: the link draws it from the port bus (a feed, −4.6 = 4.6 per unit of bus0). Read only when bus2 is set.

fields.label: Port 3 efficiency
fields.help: Flow on port 3 per unit drawn from bus0. Positive: the port bus receives it (CHP heat, 0.4 = 0.4 MWh per MWh of fuel). Negative: the link draws it from the port bus (a feed, −4.6 = 4.6 per unit of bus0). Read only when bus3 is set.

fields.label: Port 4 efficiency
fields.help: Flow on port 4 per unit drawn from bus0. Positive: the port bus receives it (CHP heat, 0.4 = 0.4 MWh per MWh of fuel). Negative: the link draws it from the port bus (a feed, −4.6 = 4.6 per unit of bus0). Read only when bus4 is set.

fields.label: Minimum flow
fields.help: Lowest flow as a share of capacity. Negative lets the link run backwards (−100 % for a bidirectional DC line).

fields.label: Maximum flow
fields.help: Highest flow as a share of capacity. A profile uploaded on the Time Series page replaces this value hour by hour.

fields.label: Unit commitment
fields.help: Model on/off decisions with start-ups and minimum up and down times. Adds integer variables: slower, more realistic for thermal plants.

fields.label: Ramp-up limit
fields.help: Largest hour-on-hour increase, as a share of capacity per hour.

fields.label: Ramp-down limit
fields.help: Largest hour-on-hour decrease, as a share of capacity per hour.

fields.label: Minimum up time
fields.help: Hours the unit stays on after a start-up.

fields.label: Minimum down time
fields.help: Hours the unit stays off after a shut-down.

fields.label: Throughput unit
fields.help: Display only: the unit of the product the unit makes per hour, for example t/h. The solve reads the efficiency, not this.

fields.label: Specific energy
fields.help: Display only, derived: electricity per tonne of product, from the efficiency. The solve reads the efficiency, not this.

fields.label: Rated apparent power
fields.help: Rated apparent power of the drive or heater, for the harmonic screen. Leave empty when unknown: the check then reads unknown. It is never taken from the capacity.

fields.label: Harmonic source
fields.help: The drive topology or heater control that sets the unit's harmonic currents. linear declares no harmonic emission. Leave empty when unknown: the check then reads unknown.

fields.label: Harmonic spectrum
fields.help: Harmonic current per order, as order:% of rated current, e.g. 5:20, 7:14. Leave empty to use the demo default for the harmonic source.

fields.label: Spectrum includes the unit's filter
fields.help: Tick when the harmonic spectrum is measured or quoted after the unit's own harmonic filter.

fields.label: Single-phase share
fields.help: The share of the unit's rated apparent power drawn between two phases or phase to neutral, for the unbalance screen. 0 declares a balanced three-phase load. Leave empty when unknown: the check then reads unknown.

fields.label: Forced-outage rate
fields.help: Share of time the asset is out on a forced outage, e.g. 5 %. Empty uses the carrier's library default. Read by the adequacy and FMEA analysis only; the dispatch is unaffected.

fields.label: Outage-rate basis
fields.help: What the rate is: FOR (service-hours based, what NERC GADS class averages publish) or EFORd (demand based). They differ materially for peakers with reserve-shutdown hours; the tool stores which one you entered and never converts between them.

fields.label: Mean time to repair
fields.help: How long one forced outage lasts on average. With the rate it implies an event frequency (8760 × rate / MTTR per year).

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique load identifier. Time-series profiles are matched to this exact name.

fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: Energy carrier of the demand (AC, heat, H2, …). Used for grouping.

fields.label: Bus
fields.help: Bus the demand is drawn from.

fields.label: Demand
fields.help: Active-power demand. A profile uploaded on the Time Series page replaces this static value hour by hour.

fields.label: Reactive demand
fields.help: Reactive-power demand, used by the AC power flow only.

fields.label: Sign
fields.help: Power sign convention: −1 for a consumer (the default), +1 to make the load inject power.

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique shunt identifier.

fields.label: Bus
fields.help: Bus the shunt connects to ground.

fields.label: Conductance
fields.help: Shunt conductance; absorbs active power in the AC power flow.

fields.label: Susceptance
fields.help: Shunt susceptance; positive injects reactive power (a capacitor), negative absorbs it (a reactor).

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique storage unit identifier. Time-series profiles are matched to this exact name.

fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: Storage technology (battery, PHS, …). Used for grouping; does not change the energy balance.

fields.label: Bus
fields.help: Bus the storage charges from and discharges to.

fields.label: Power
fields.help: Charge and discharge rating on the AC side.

fields.label: Duration
fields.help: Hours of storage at rated power: energy = power × duration.

fields.label: Extendable
fields.help: When ticked, the optimiser chooses the capacity between the minimum and maximum and pays the annualised cost for every MW it adds.

fields.label: Minimum capacity
fields.help: Lower bound on the optimised capacity. Set it to the existing capacity to forbid retirement.

fields.label: Maximum capacity
fields.help: Upper bound on the optimised capacity. Leave empty for no limit.

fields.label: Power part: overnight cost
fields.help: Upfront cost of the power conversion (inverter, grid connection) per kW of power.

fields.label: Power part: lifetime
fields.help: Lifetime of the power part. When shorter than the energy part's, finance books a replacement.

fields.label: Energy part: overnight cost
fields.help: Upfront cost of the storage block per kWh of energy.

fields.label: Energy part: lifetime
fields.help: Lifetime of the storage block.

fields.label: Build year
fields.help: First year the asset operates. With its lifetime, it decides in which investment periods the asset exists.

fields.label: Discount rate
fields.help: The rate this asset's overnight cost is annualised at. Leave empty to use the project's rate from Solver Settings.

fields.label: Lifetime
fields.help: Derived: the longest part lifetime, the one the asset retires with.

fields.label: Capital cost (annualised)
fields.help: Derived from both parts: each part's overnight cost annualised over its own lifetime, the energy part scaled by the duration; fixed O&M is charged on top. Per kW of power.

fields.label: Power part: fixed O&M
fields.help: Fixed O&M of the power part, as a share of its overnight cost per year.

fields.label: Energy part: fixed O&M
fields.help: Fixed O&M of the storage block, as a share of its overnight cost per year.

fields.label: Fixed O&M (total)
fields.help: Derived: both parts' fixed O&M per kW of power per year.

fields.label: Marginal cost
fields.help: Cost per MWh dispatched, e.g. to model wear.

fields.label: Charging efficiency
fields.help: Share of the electricity drawn that reaches the store.

fields.label: Discharging efficiency
fields.help: Share of the stored energy delivered as electricity.

fields.label: Standing loss
fields.help: Share of the state of charge lost each hour (self-discharge).

fields.label: Cyclic state of charge
fields.help: The state of charge at the end must equal the start, so the model cannot start with free energy.

fields.label: Initial state of charge
fields.help: Energy in the store at the first snapshot. Ignored when the state of charge is cyclic.

fields.label: Inflow
fields.help: Energy flowing into the store from outside, e.g. river inflow for hydro. Upload a profile on the Time Series page for hourly values.

fields.label: Forced-outage rate
fields.help: Share of time the asset is out on a forced outage, e.g. 5 %. Empty uses the carrier's library default. Read by the adequacy and FMEA analysis only; the dispatch is unaffected.

fields.label: Outage-rate basis
fields.help: What the rate is: FOR (service-hours based, what NERC GADS class averages publish) or EFORd (demand based). They differ materially for peakers with reserve-shutdown hours; the tool stores which one you entered and never converts between them.

fields.label: Mean time to repair
fields.help: How long one forced outage lasts on average. With the rate it implies an event frequency (8760 × rate / MTTR per year).

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique store identifier. Time-series profiles are matched to this exact name.

fields.label: Carrier
fields.help: Energy carrier held (H2, heat, battery, …). Used for grouping; does not change the energy balance.

fields.label: Bus
fields.help: Bus the store exchanges energy with. It has no power limit of its own: the Links and other components on that bus set the charge and discharge rate.

fields.label: Energy capacity
fields.help: Energy the store can hold. With extendable ticked, the existing capacity the optimiser starts from.

fields.label: Extendable
fields.help: When ticked, the optimiser chooses the energy capacity between the minimum and maximum and pays the annualised cost for every MWh it adds.

fields.label: Minimum capacity
fields.help: Lower bound on the optimised energy capacity.

fields.label: Maximum capacity
fields.help: Upper bound on the optimised energy capacity. Leave empty for no limit.

fields.label: Overnight cost
fields.help: Upfront cost per kWh of storage capacity, as if built at once without financing. Annualised over the lifetime at the discount rate.

fields.label: Lifetime
fields.help: Technical and economic lifetime. The store retires after its build year plus lifetime.

fields.label: Build year
fields.help: First year the asset operates. With its lifetime, it decides in which investment periods the asset exists.

fields.label: Discount rate
fields.help: The rate this asset's overnight cost is annualised at. Leave empty to use the project's rate from Solver Settings.

fields.label: Capital cost (annualised)
fields.help: Derived: overnight cost × annuity(discount rate, lifetime); fixed O&M is charged on top. Per kWh of capacity.

fields.label: Fixed O&M
fields.help: Fixed operation and maintenance per kWh of capacity per year.

fields.label: Marginal cost
fields.help: Cost per MWh discharged.

fields.label: Minimum state of energy
fields.help: Lowest allowed fill level, as a share of the energy capacity.

fields.label: Maximum state of energy
fields.help: Highest allowed fill level, as a share of the energy capacity.

fields.label: Cyclic state of energy
fields.help: The fill level at the end must equal the start, so the model cannot start with free energy.

fields.label: Initial energy
fields.help: Energy in the store at the first snapshot. Ignored when the state of energy is cyclic.

fields.label: Standing loss
fields.help: Share of the stored energy lost each hour (self-discharge, boil-off).

fields.label: Forced-outage rate
fields.help: Share of time the asset is out on a forced outage, e.g. 5 %. Empty uses the carrier's library default. Read by the adequacy and FMEA analysis only; the dispatch is unaffected.

fields.label: Outage-rate basis
fields.help: What the rate is: FOR (service-hours based, what NERC GADS class averages publish) or EFORd (demand based). They differ materially for peakers with reserve-shutdown hours; the tool stores which one you entered and never converts between them.

fields.label: Mean time to repair
fields.help: How long one forced outage lasts on average. With the rate it implies an event frequency (8760 × rate / MTTR per year).

fields.label: Name
fields.help: Unique transformer identifier.

fields.label: HV bus
fields.help: The bus at one end. A positive flow in the results runs from this bus to the other.

fields.label: LV bus
fields.help: The bus at the other end.

fields.label: Capacity
fields.help: Apparent-power rating of the transformer. With extendable ticked, the existing capacity the optimiser starts from.

fields.label: Extendable
fields.help: When ticked, the optimiser chooses the capacity between the minimum and maximum and pays the annualised cost for every MVA it adds.

fields.label: Minimum capacity
fields.help: Lower bound on the optimised capacity.

fields.label: Maximum capacity
fields.help: Upper bound on the optimised capacity. Leave empty for no limit.

fields.label: Overnight cost
fields.help: Upfront cost per MVA of rating, as if built at once without financing. Annualised over the lifetime at the discount rate.

fields.label: Lifetime
fields.help: Technical and economic lifetime. The transformer retires after its build year plus lifetime; leave empty for never.

fields.label: Build year
fields.help: First year the asset operates. With its lifetime, it decides in which investment periods the asset exists.

fields.label: Discount rate
fields.help: The rate this asset's overnight cost is annualised at. Leave empty to use the project's rate from Solver Settings.

fields.label: Capital cost (annualised)
fields.help: Derived: overnight cost × annuity(discount rate, lifetime); fixed O&M is charged on top. Per MVA of rating.

fields.label: Fixed O&M
fields.help: Fixed operation and maintenance per MVA of rating per year.

fields.label: Declared HV voltage
fields.help: Nominal voltage of the HV winding. Checked against the HV bus.

fields.label: Declared LV voltage
fields.help: Nominal voltage of the LV winding. Checked against the LV bus.

fields.label: Resistance
fields.help: Series resistance in per unit of the rating.

fields.label: Reactance
fields.help: Series reactance in per unit of the rating.

fields.label: Tap ratio
fields.help: Off-nominal turns ratio (1 = nominal).

fields.label: Phase shift
fields.help: Phase shift between the windings.
